material.text: opencode-gearbox: Gearbox for OpenCode: picks the reasoning effort and model for every prompt and every subagent.

type=plugin source=npm:opencode-gearbox created=2026-11-11T13:07:12.591Z firstSeen=2026-11-12T16:45:49.889Z published=2026-11-13T09:55:50.946Z maintainers=miguelmartens repoId=1453818025 stars=4 npm30d=?

Automatic transmission for OpenCode.

Gearbox picks the reasoning effort for every prompt and every subagent,
and the cheapest model that fits each subagent. You stop shifting by hand.

Website · Install · Models · Gears · Commands · Board · Options · Judge · Model switching

--- ## Why You pick a variant, forget it, and burn `max` effort on `rename this variable`. Or you leave it on `low` and the hard bug gets a shallow answer. Subagents inherit your most expensive model even when they only grep. Gearbox fixes that. A small judge model rates each prompt. Gearbox shifts the effort for the turn and gives each subagent its own level and a cheaper model when it fits. A status bar shows what it chose and why. ``` ⚙ high · haiku-5-5 · ◔ 38% · cache 4:12 · Auto ``` Gearbox is built for **Claude models** first; other models with effort variants work too (see [Supported models](#supported-models)). It is an OpenCode plugin and does not run in Claude Code. It was inspired by [HeyCubit/effortless](https://github.com/HeyCubit/effortless), a Claude Code mod, but written from scratch for OpenCode V2. ## The five gears

| Gear | Level | Typical prompt | Subagent model on the ladder | Expected output | | :--: | -------- | ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------: | | 1 | `low` | Renames, lookups, one-line fixes | cheapest | 800 tokens | | 2 | `medium` | Everyday edits; also the fallback | middle | 3 000 tokens | | 3 | `high` | Debugging across files | the chat model | 8 000 tokens | | 4 | `xhigh` | Refactors, design trade-offs | the chat model | 16 000 tokens | | 5 | `max` | Full reasoning, or say "max effort" | the chat model | 32 000 tokens | The "typical prompt" column is a guide; [the judge decides](#how-the-judge-decides). ## What it does - **Auto effort.** The judge rates each main-chat prompt `low | medium | high | xhigh | max`. Gearbox applies that level as the model's matching variant settings on every request of the turn. - **Subagents.** Each task-tool subagent gets its own level. By default it also gets a model from your provider's price ladder on its first prompt, because a fresh subagent has no cache to lose. A subagent whose agent file sets `model` keeps that model; Gearbox only sets its effort. - **No judge for the obvious cases.** Follow-ups (`ok`, `go`, `yes please`, `continue`) reuse the last level. A read-only `explore` subagent runs at `low`, so it starts without waiting for the judge. "max effort", "low effort" and the other level names in a prompt set that level directly, unless a negation comes just before ("no need for max effort"). - **Never in your way.** If you pick a variant yourself, Gearbox pauses for that session and tells you once. A judge timeout, an unreadable answer or a provider error falls back to the last level, else `medium`. The judge never blocks a prompt. - **Context care.** - Compaction summaries are written by the judge model (see [Pick a fast judge](#pick-a-fast-judge)) when that is cheaper than the session's own compaction and the conversation fits the judge's context. A warm session cache can make the session's model cheaper; then OpenCode compacts as usual. A judge summary that takes over 30 s also falls back to OpenCode. The summary model receives the whole conversation; a judge model picked automatically is always on the session's provider (see [Pick a fast judge](#pick-a-fast-judge)). - `/gearbox handoff` starts a fresh session seeded with a summary. - A warning when the context gets swamped. - Handoff advice when the work has moved on. - **Stats, save mode and budget.** - Per session: user turns per level, model requests, tokens, cost and judge cost. - Save mode caps effort for a few hours. - An optional daily spend budget turns save mode on at 80%. It counts the cost each provider reports per request. A reported cost of 0 (subscriptions) is trusted, so on those providers only judge calls add to the spend. - **Benchmark.** `/gearbox bench` scores a judge model on 135 labelled prompts: 75 from effortless and 60 of Gearbox's own (subagent tasks, edge-case-heavy work, pasted logs, prompt injection). ## Benchmark | Setup | Solved | Output tokens / task | Cost / task | Time / task | Cost vs always-high | | --------------------- | -------: | -------------------: | ----------: | ----------: | ------------------: | | always medium | 100% | 2.4k | $0.1 | 24 s | −16% | | always high | 98% | 3.6k | $0.12 | 32 s | baseline | | always xhigh | 98% | 7.3k | $0.18 | 58 s | +47% | | gearbox · effort only | 96% | 3.4k | $0.12 | 31 s | −4% | | **gearbox auto** | **100%** | **3.9k** | **$0.12** | **34 s** | **−4%** | 24 tasks × 2 runs · model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 · judge anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5#none · OpenCode 2.2.6 · Gearbox 0.4.1 · 2026-11-12 · medians, judge cost included. [Method and raw data](bench/README.md) ## Supported models Gearbox works per model, not per provider. A model is supported when its OpenCode catalog entry has at least one effort variant named after a level (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`). Gearbox copies the chosen variant's settings into each request, so it speaks whatever API the model uses. Only Claude models usually have all five levels. Many GPT, DeepSeek and other models stop at `high`, or offer only some levels. When the model lacks the judged level, Gearbox uses the nearest lower variant. If there is no lower one, it uses the nearest higher one. For example, on a model with `low`, `medium` and `high`: | Judged level | Variant sent | | ----------------- | ------------ | | `low` … `high` | the same | | `xhigh` and `max` | `high` | On a model with only `high` and `max`, a `low` turn runs on `high`. The status bar shows both, e.g. `xhigh→high`. `/gearbox stats` counts the turn at the judged level, and `/gearbox debug` shows the variant actually sent. Variants such as `none`, `minimal` and `thinking` are never used for effort. | Models | API | Status on OpenCode 2.2.6 | | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | | **Claude** (e.g. `claude-haiku-5-5`) | Anthropic Messages (`output_config`) | **Primary target.** Verified, and the recommended judge | | GPT (e.g. `gpt-6-luna`) | OpenAI Responses (`reasoning.effort`) | Verified | | DeepSeek and other OpenAI-compatible | OpenAI-compatible (`reasoning_effort`) | Verified | | Gemini, Mistral | Google (`thinkingConfig`), Mistral | Should work; unverified | | Any model without effort variants | any | Runs unchanged; the bar says `Paused: no effort control` | What "Claude first" means: - The end-to-end run and the judge benchmark used Claude through the `opencode-go` provider. Claude through `anthropic` or any other provider that speaks Anthropic Messages gets the same treatment. - The recommended judge is a Claude Haiku model with thinking off (`#none`); it scored 71/75 on the effortless set at about 1 s per answer. - The 5-minute default cache TTL in the status bar matches Anthropic. For other providers it is an assumption; set `settings.cache.ttl` to correct it. - Model switching for subagents needs model prices. Subscription catalogs without prices give effort control only. ## Install **Requirements:** OpenCode **V2, 2.2.6 or later** (V1 is not supported). Bun 1.4 or later only to develop and run the tests. Add the package to the `plugins` list of your global (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`) or project `opencode.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["opencode-gearbox"], } ``` To set options, use the object form: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "opencode-gearbox", "options": { "judge": { "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5#none" }, "bias": 1 }, }, ], } ``` OpenCode reloads its plugins when you save the config, so no restart is needed. The TUI status bar ships in the same package and loads with it. To run it from a checkout, use the absolute path of the repository instead of the package name. The path must be a directory. ### Pick a fast judge The judge must answer within `judge.timeoutMs` (4 s by default), or the turn falls back to the last level. The same model writes compaction and handoff summaries. Gearbox uses, in order: 1. `judge.model`. 2. Your `small_model` (V2 stores it as the `title` agent's model), when it is on the session's provider. Prompts never go to another provider unless you name that model in `judge.model`. 3. The cheapest tool-capable model of the session's provider. 4. The session's own model. For options 2–4, Gearbox picks the model's `none`, `minimal` or `low` variant when it has one, so the judge does not think for long. An explicit `judge.model` is used as given: add the variant yourself, e.g. `#none`. Run `/gearbox bench` for your judge, and `/gearbox bench provider/model` for a candidate, before you rely on it. In the end-to-end run on `opencode-go`, `claude-haiku-5-5#none` scored 71/75 on the effortless set at about 1 s per answer; the Gearbox set has no published run yet. `deepseek-v4.1-flash` was often overloaded and missed the 4 s timeout. See `test/e2e/CHECKLIST.md`. ## Try it After you install Gearbox, open the TUI in any project and watch the status bar while you work through these steps. The judge decides, so your levels can differ by a step. 1. **A small task.** Send `rename the variable x to count`. The bar shows `low` or `medium`. 2. **A hard task.** Send `debug why the tests fail across these modules`. The bar shows `high` or above. 3. **A named level.** Send `max effort: review this design`. The bar shows `max`, and no judge call is made. 4. **A follow-up.** Send `ok`. Gearbox reuses the last level without the judge. 5. **Your own pick.** Choose a variant by hand. The bar shows `Paused: manual variant`. Run `/gearbox auto on` to hand control back. 6. **A subagent.** Ask for work that starts a subagent, e.g. `use a subagent to find every TODO`. Its first request runs on a cheaper model from the ladder when your provider lists prices. 7. **The numbers.** Run `/gearbox stats` for turns, tokens and cost, `/gearbox debug` for the last decision, and `/gearbox bench` to score your judge. ## Commands All output appears as a toast or, for long text, as a dialog. No model turn is started. | Command | What it does | | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `/gearbox` | Status: level, model, mode, reason, context, save mode, today's spend | | `/gearbox help` | The command list | | `/gearbox auto on\|off` | Automatic effort on or off. `on` also resumes a session paused by a manual variant | | `/gearbox set ` | Change a setting, e.g. `set bias -1`, `set judge.model openai/gpt-6-luna#none`, `set judge.model null` | | `/gearbox settings` | Show the current settings | | `/gearbox save [on\|off]` | Cap effort at `saveMode.cap` for `saveMode.hours` | | `/gearbox stats` | User turns per level, model requests, tokens, cost and judge cost for this session | | `/gearbox bench [set] [p/m]` | Score the judge model (or `provider/model[#variant]`) on the labelled prompts: `effortless`, `gearbox` or both; see [Judge cases](#judge-cases) | | `/gearbox handoff [full]` | Continue in a fresh session seeded with a summary. `full` also writes `HANDOFF.md` | | `/gearbox compact [note]` | Compact now; the summary keeps `note` in mind, whether the judge model or OpenCode writes it | | `/gearbox debug` | Last decision, the judge's raw answer, whether a judge call is running, and the last request's model | | `/gearbox board` | Write the [board](#board), a local page of every session and project, and open it in the browser | Plugin commands run from the TUI (or `client.session.command`). `opencode run "/gearbox …"` sends the text as a normal prompt. In `/gearbox stats` a **turn** is one user prompt, counted once at the level Gearbox set for it. A turn Gearbox did not route (auto off, paused by a manual variant, or a model without effort control) counts as **manual**. A …[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]… | | ---------------- | ----: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Effort signals | 32 | edge cases, risky domains, brownfield/greenfield pairs, changes across layers, fully specified work, sketches, verify passes, unattended runs, critical work | | Gearbox's inputs | 14 | subagent tasks, urgency words written by a parent model, short replies to the previous answer, the same prompt at 5% and 85% context | | Traps | 14 | long pasted logs, prompt injection, talk about effort, dramatic wording on small jobs, German, Spanish and Japanese | Every `gearbox` case reaches the judge in production: none is a follow-up or names a level. Its cases pass the previous reply, the subagent flag and the context share to the judge exactly as Gearbox does while you work. ### How a case is scored - **Hit:** the judged level is one of the case's acceptable levels (one level, or two adjacent ones). - **Holdout:** 20 cases in each set were written before any judge prompt was tuned and are never tuned against. The bench reports them on their own line; that is the honest score. - **Misses** are split into too low and too high. Too low risks the work and too high only costs more, so too-low steps count double in the miss cost, and answers 2 or more levels too low are counted apart. - **Never judged in production:** the bench lists the cases that Gearbox's rules handle before the judge (7 in the effortless set). They are still scored, to stay comparable with upstream. - A failed judge call (timeout or provider error) is retried once. Cases still unanswered are listed apart from wrong answers. - Bench calls are real spend: they count in today's spend (and the budget), and the bench output shows their cost, but they stay out of the session's stats. ### Known limits - **Small sets.** At 60 cases, 51/60 means somewhere between 74% and 92%. Only large differences between two judges show. Judges are not deterministic either: run the bench 3 times before you compare. - **The `effortless` set is near its ceiling.** Upstream judges score 92–99% on it, so it shows regressions better than improvements. - **The `gearbox` labels are one view.** Gearbox's author labelled them with a written guide; a blind second labeller agreed on 59 of 60 cases, but it was a Claude model too. A labeller from another model family is still to do. - **Labels are not outcomes.** A hit means the judge agrees with the label, not that the level solved the task faster or cheaper. The task benchmark in [`bench/`](bench/README.md) measures outcomes. [`bench/judge-cases.md`](bench/judge-cases.md) has the field reference, the level meanings, the labelling rules and how to compare two judges. ## How model switching decides Gearbox only switches between models of the session's own provider and never picks a model above the session's own model. **The ladder.** - **Who is on it:** every enabled, tool-capable model of the provider whose id matches `effortModels`. - **Price limit:** its output price is at or below the chat model's. Models without a price (subscription catalogs with an empty `cost`) are left out. - **No outdated models:** a model is left out when a newer model of the same family (OpenCode's `family`, e.g. `claude-haiku`) costs no more and offers effort control too. Of two aliases with the same price and date, one stays. For example, under `claude-sonnet-5-5` the ladder is `claude-haiku-5-5`, then `claude-sonnet-5-5`: `claude-haiku-4-5` and `claude-sonnet-5` are left out. - **Order:** cheapest first, with the chat model last. **Which rung a level gets.** - `low` → the cheapest model. - `medium` → the middle of the ladder. - `high`, `xhigh`, `max` → the chat model itself. **Subagents** (`modelSwitch.subagents`, on by default). A subagent's model can only change in its prompt hook. So in a child session Gearbox waits for the judge there, at most `judge.timeoutMs` in total, session and catalog reads included. - **First prompt:** the child has no cache yet, so Gearbox switches it to the ladder model with the matching variant. - **Later prompts** (a resumed subagent): the child holds a warm cache. Gearbox changes its model only when the cost check below (with `minSavingRatio`) says switching is cheaper than staying. So a resumed child never climbs to a pricier model; its effort still follows the level. - **Effort rungs first:** the subagent ladder skips cheaper models without effort variants, unless no model on it has any. - **No effort above the level:** it also skips cheaper models whose lowest effort variant is above the level, e.g. a model with only `high` and `max` for a `medium` subagent. - **Your pick wins:** an agent with its own `model` keeps it. While the root session runs on a variant you picked (and you have not run `/gearbox auto on`), its subagents are left alone too. - **No model of its own:** a subagent whose session has no model is routed from its nearest ancestor's model, else from OpenCode's default model. If that ancestor runs on a picked variant, the subagent keeps it. A free or "contributor" model at the bottom of the ladder may not suit you; leave it out with `effortModels`, e.g. `"^(?!.*free).*$"`. **Main chat.** Gearbox never switches the main chat's model; it sets effort only. **The cost check** (resumed subagents; the cache counts as warm only on the model that served the last request): - Staying costs `context × (warm ? cache-read price : input price) + expected output × output price`. - Switching costs `context × cache-write price (else input price) + expected output × the target's output price`. - Gearbox switches only when switching costs at most `1 − minSavingRatio` of staying. Expected output per level is 800, 3 000, 8 000, 16 000 and 32 000 tokens. **OpenCode 2.2.6 limits.** - 2.2.6 does not fire the `experimental.model.resolve` hook, the only place a main-chat switch could happen per request. So the main chat gets effort only. Gearbox does not register the hook; main-chat switching will be built and probed against a release that fires it. - Effort goes through the `context` hook on every agent-loop step. Gearbox copies the chosen variant's settings into the request options, e.g. `output_config.effort` on Anthropic and `reasoning.effort` on OpenAI. ## Development ``` bun install bun test # tests bun run format:check # formatting bun run check # both ``` - `src/core/`: pure decisions, with no OpenCode imports. - `src/server/`: the OpenCode V2 hooks. - `src/tui/`: the status bar. - `docs/api-probe.md`: the verified OpenCode V2 API facts. - `docs/adr/`: architecture decision records ([guidance](https://architecture-decision-record.github.io/en-us/)). - `test/e2e/CHECKLIST.md`: the manual end-to-end run against a real OpenCode. ## Brand Logo, emblems and banners live in [`assets/brand/`](assets/brand). They are free to use when you write or talk about Gearbox. Show that your project runs on it: ```md [![Shifted by Gearbox](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelmartens/opencode-gearbox/main/assets/brand/badge-shifted-by-gearbox.svg)](https://github.com/miguelmartens/opencode-gearbox) ``` ## Credits - The 75 labelled benchmark prompts in `bench/effortless-judge-cases.json` come from [HeyCubit/effortless](https://github.com/HeyCubit/effortless) (MIT). They were taken via [tehchaoz/effortless-opencode](https://github.com/tehchaoz/effortless-opencode) (MIT). See [NOTICE.md](./NOTICE.md). - No code is shared with either project. - The labels of Gearbox's own 60 prompts (`bench/gearbox-judge-cases.json`) follow Anthropic's [Spending your effort](https://claude.dev/blog/spending-your-effort/) and the [effort docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort). ## License MIT © Miguel Martens. # Notice

opencode-gearbox is original work under the root `LICENSE`, except for the
benchmark data listed below. It is inspired by HeyCubit/effortless (a Claude
Code mod) but shares no code with it or with effortless-opencode.

## Benchmark prompts

`bench/effortless-judge-cases.json` holds the 75 labelled judge prompts written for
<https://github.com/HeyCubit/effortless> (MIT). The file was taken verbatim from
<https://github.com/tehchaoz/effortless-opencode> (`parity/judge-cases.json`,
commit `ad2596683fe9e2be8aceebe974316a97327868e9`) and renamed; its contents are
unchanged. effortless-opencode is an OpenCode port of HeyCubit/effortless that
reuses the original's labelled prompts under MIT.
